# Google Vids Gets Custom Captions and More Natural AI Voices

> **In short:** Google says Vids now lets you fully customize caption style — font, position, and animation — and has upgraded its AI voiceover to sound more natural and generate audio faster. Both are available now on supported plans.

You've probably scrolled past a video on mute, kept watching because the captions looked good, and clicked away the second they felt generic. That's the kind of detail Google is trying to fix in Vids, its video creation tool — with two updates going out at the same time.

## Captions you can actually style

Until now, Vids captions came in one fixed look. Google says you can now change the font, the typography (the visual styling — bold, size, that kind of thing), where the captions sit on the screen, and how they animate as they appear.

Why bother? Captions are how most people follow videos on social feeds, in offices, or anywhere the sound is off. Captions that match your brand colors or your video's mood help a video feel finished — and stop viewers from scrolling past.

Google specifically calls out two groups most likely to care: marketing and social teams who need captions to match brand fonts and colors across ads and promo videos, and creators who want animated, eye-catching captions to make short videos more engaging on feeds.

## AI voiceovers that sound less robotic

The other update is less visible but you'll hear it. Google says the text-to-speech engine (TTS, or the AI that turns written words into spoken audio) behind Vids' voiceover has been upgraded. According to Google, the new engine brings better sentence flow, more lifelike pacing, and "context-aware emphasis" — meaning the AI stresses the right words at the right moments instead of reading everything at the same flat volume. Google also says the audio generates faster, so you can preview your voiceover in real time as you tweak the script.

For anyone who's used an AI voice tool before, the practical change is simple: the result sounds less like a robot reading a teleprompter, and more like a person who knows what they're talking about.

## Who can use these right now

Google says both updates are available now on Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains, and that no admin setup is required. The captions update is rolling out across Google's Business, Enterprise, Education, and several Consumer plans. The voiceover upgrade covers a similar set of Business, Enterprise, Education, and Consumer plans, including Google AI Pro and Ultra.

Neither feature has a dedicated admin toggle, so the Help Center is the place to look for exactly where the controls live in your workspace.

## What this means for you

- **If you're making videos for marketing or social media:** Custom captions are a small thing that can lift a video from "draft" to "ready to post." Spend five minutes matching your brand font and color before the next campaign goes out.
- **If you create training, internal, or explainer videos at work:** A more natural AI voice means you can record scripts without booking a studio. Re-record your last video and you'll likely notice the difference immediately.
- **If you make videos for fun or as a hobby:** Animated captions and a less robotic voice make short social videos feel more polished — and they help when your audience is watching on mute in a waiting room.
- **If you already use it:** A useful next step is to re-run an old project with the new voice engine — that's the fastest way to hear what's changed, before you build anything new.

## Wrap-up

Captions and voice are the two details that decide whether a video feels finished or feels like a rough draft. Google says both just got meaningful upgrades in Vids. If you want to see whether the changes matter to your work, open Vids, pick an old project, and try the new caption style and voice on a short test clip — that should tell you within a few minutes whether it's worth using for your next video.
